President of the United States from 1961 to 1963. He was the youngest person ever elected president and the first Catholic.

From a rich Boston family, he served as a navy officer in World War II, then as a congressman and senator. He narrowly beat Richard Nixon in 1960.

His presidency was shaped by the Cold War:

  • 1961: a CIA-backed invasion of Cuba at the Bay of Pigs failed badly.
  • 1961: he set the goal of landing a man on the Moon by the end of the decade, which led to the Moon landing of 1969.
  • 1962: in the Cuban Missile Crisis he forced the Soviet Union to remove nuclear missiles from Cuba, the closest the world came to nuclear war.
  • 1963: he signed a treaty with the Soviets and Britain banning nuclear tests in the air, in space and under water.

He sent more military advisers to Vietnam. In 1963 he proposed a civil rights law, passed after his death as the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

He was shot dead in Dallas on 22 November 1963. Vice President Lyndon B. Johnson took over.
sum: President of the United States from 1961 to 1963. He was the youngest person ever elected president and the first Catholic.
